name: AstridProtocol
fix_description: In withdraw, the _restakedTokenAddress parameter is not validated against the whitelist (unlike deposit which checks stakedTokenMapping.whitelisted). Attacker passes a malicious token contract that manipulates scaledBalanceOf to inflate shares. Fix: add whitelist validation for _restakedTokenAddress in withdraw, same as deposit.
difficulty_reasoning: The exploit is a very straightforward fake-token/input-validation flaw: deploy malicious ERC20s that spoof the expected restaked token interface, call withdraw and claim for each supported asset, then swap proceeds to ETH. It is only a few simple steps with obvious malicious contract setup and minimal protocol-specific reasoning beyond understanding the vulnerable contract trusts attacker-controlled token metadata.
